definitions.meaning: a swarming insect that strips crops bare
the false acacia or carob, a tree known by the same name as the insect

explanation.surface: Some creature is chewing up the plants inside a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the crop-stripping grasshopper and the robinia or carob tree share the name.

clue.text: Fail to reckon with clue — not so devious!

indicators.note: devious means winding and indirect, so these letters take a crooked route into a new order

explanation.surface: A solver complains that the setter's clue should have been less tricky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devious' rearranges CLUE plus NOT SO; the exclamation pretends to plead with the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing track of a tally is an idiom for failing to keep a numerical reckoning.

clue.text: One found in song and another one in wine

indicators.note: found in says the first letter goes inside the word for song

parts.note: a chant is a song
I is the Roman numeral for one
a second Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A singer spots a couple of things, one in a song, one in a wine glass.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuscan red named after its home region is a well-known Italian wine.

clue.text: Like Concorde thus carrying posh sort

indicators.note: carrying means the word for thus holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used in quotations
U is the old shorthand for upper-class usage
a sort, as in a good sort, is a person

explanation.surface: Concorde's passengers were posh sorts, so it is apt that the plane carried one.
explanation.definitionFit: The airliner flew faster than the speed of sound, its famous distinction.

clue.text: Provincial Pope on vehicle turned back

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means placed after, so the Pope comes second, after the vehicle
turned back says the vehicle's word is written in reverse

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
Urban was the name of eight popes

explanation.surface: A pontiff riding a vehicle that has turned around, seemingly in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Outskirts-of-town life is often called narrow or unsophisticated, the sense of provincial.

clue.text: One has confidence in this investment

parts.note: a unit is one
to trust is to have confidence in

explanation.surface: An investor is described as having faith in a particular fund.
explanation.definitionFit: This pooled fund is a common type of investment in which savers buy units.

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pushy editor took advantage of somebody.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit someone is to take advantage of them, a close synonym of the past participle.

clue.text: One involved in main takeover bid?

definitions.text: One involved in main takeover bid?

parts.words: One involved in main takeover bid?
parts.note: the main is the open sea, and a takeover bid there is a pirate attack on a ship, whose attackers climb aboard

explanation.surface: Reads like a description of a corporate raider in a major takeover battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' suggests 'principal' and 'takeover bid' the City; in fact it is the sea and a ship being stormed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone storming a vessel by climbing onto its deck is the person who goes aboard it.

clue.text: It's unacceptable whichever way you look at it

definitions.note: the phrase meaning beyond the pale is a two-word negative idiom that reads identically backwards

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: whichever way you look at it says the letters read the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: the phrase meaning beyond the pale is a two-word negative idiom that reads identically backwards

explanation.surface: Someone declares that something is wrong from every angle.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for behaviour that crosses the line means it is not acceptable.

clue.text: Grumpy type Republican bundled into taxi

indicators.note: bundled into means pushed inside, so the letter goes within the taxi

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A political figure is hustled into a cab, presumably grumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: A crabby, irritable person is called by the name of the sideways-walking crustacean.

clue.text: One in doze succeeded first as team leader

indicators.note: first places the letter for succeeded at the front

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies
a kipper is jokingly one who kips, that is takes a doze

explanation.surface: A sleepy player won through first to become captain.
explanation.definitionFit: The captain of a sports team is often called its skipper.

parts.note: a fire that is still in is still alight
to exact is to demand

explanation.surface: A passenger is ordered to step down from a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get off' looks like one phrase meaning alight; 'to get' is the link and 'off' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure that is off is slightly wrong or not precise.

clue.text: Have say in vote against payment

parts.note: a con is a vote or argument against, as in pros and cons
a tribute was a payment made by a subject state

explanation.surface: Citizens want a voice in deciding whether to oppose a levy.
explanation.definitionFit: To play a part in a discussion or decision is to add your input, synonym of having a say.

indicators.note: in says the name sits inside the following words, straddling them

explanation.surface: A politician is found inside a walled garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walled enclosure' suggests the biblical garden, the answer itself, but it is only the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Anthony, Conservative Prime Minister at the time of Suez in 1956, is the statesman meant.

parts.note: to tender is to offer
to foot it is to dance

explanation.surface: A novice invites someone onto the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer unused to hardship, originally in the American West, is a greenhorn.

definitions.meaning: a nun's habit is an example of standard official dress

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in their ways, never altering their routines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habits' tempts as routines; it means the dress worn by monks and nuns.
explanation.definitionFit: Constant means unvarying; the noun is the regulation clothing worn by members of a group.

definitions.meaning: someone who lives by asking for alms
split into three, the word says '...', a claim that one cannot be reformed

explanation.surface: A vagrant insists there is no hope of reforming them.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendicant friars lived on alms, so the word is a formal term for a beggar.

parts.note: un is French for a
Earth is a planet

explanation.surface: An astronomer wonders about finding an alien world.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig something up or bring it to light is to find it.

definitions.meaning: people who cut and turn grass for fodder

explanation.definitionFit: A wild knockout punch shares its name with labourers who mow and dry grass in the fields.

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A critic says some writer of novels is unlike anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like part of 'novel writer'; it is the anagram signal on NOT LIKE.
explanation.definitionFit: J.R.R. Tolkien wrote The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings.

clue.text: Praise sports hall on radio, and book

indicators.note: on radio says the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: to laud is to praise; a gym is a sports hall

explanation.surface: A broadcaster commends a leisure centre and a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Jim is Joseph Conrad's 1900 novel about a disgraced sailor.

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: wide means broad
the Tay is a river in Scotland

explanation.surface: A channel runs into a wide river, as described by the Reverend Spooner.
explanation.definitionFit: The channel along which tidal water runs, especially on the Thames, is called a tideway.

clue.text: Now that could be display stand!

indicators.note: could be says the letters might form something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation, as if someone has just spotted a stand for ornaments.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian set of open shelves for ornaments is called a whatnot.

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: the heart is the centre

explanation.surface: A city centre is said to draw people in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' is not a verb: it is the plural of doe, female deer, which a stag attracts.
explanation.definitionFit: A male red deer is a stag that female deer are drawn to.

clue.text: Big hit from Ruth perhaps as poet

definitions.meaning: Babe Ruth was a US baseball star famous for hitting the ball out of the park
the Greek author of the Iliad

explanation.surface: Something Ruth wrote may be a poem that struck a chord.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball slang a home run is called a homer; Homer is also the ancient Greek epic poet.

clue.text: 19th Century stuff in article by two men

parts.note: two men's names, Victor and Ian
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Antiques from the 1800s were shown in a magazine piece written by two men.
explanation.definitionFit: Objects from the reign of Queen Victoria are collectively known by this term.

definitions.meaning: a better is one who bets; the totalisator is a betting system on racecourses
to carry, as in hauling a bag

explanation.surface: A plan for improving how people get around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like the comparative of good; it means a gambler.
explanation.definitionFit: The totalisator is pool betting at British racecourses; to tote something is to carry it.

definitions.meaning: a woman in the Women's Royal Naval Service

explanation.surface: An aviator who is not a sailor in the fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiny brown bird shares its name with members of the Women's Royal Naval Service, Britain's former women's navy branch.

parts.note: major means chief or main
CA stands for chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A finance director arrives for a holiday on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Majorca is the largest of Spain's Balearic Islands.

indicators.note: revolution means turning round, so the letters of the first word are spun into a new order

explanation.surface: A rebellion crushed by a counter-revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter-revolution' reads as one political word; it splits into fodder and anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce an opponent is to beat them soundly.

clue.text: Think there's place available in crew say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: room is space available; in gives IN; a rowing eight is a crew

explanation.surface: A rower wonders whether there's a seat free in the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, 'room in eight' gives the answer; 'crew' is a rowing eight.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruminate is to ponder or turn something over in the mind.

parts.note: a stat is a statistic, a figure
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A statue is shipped across the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing figure' suggests a statue; 'Standing' is the definition, 'figure' a statistic.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's status is their rank or position in society.
